The search turned up several GitHub threads on this. None shows an upstream React fix. The usual workaround is `suppressHydrationWarning` on `<html>` or `<body>`, or disabling the extension.

- **ColorZilla in Next.js:** Next.js issues #72031 and #72035 trace the error to a `cz-shortcut-listen` attribute the extension adds before hydration. A Next.js maintainer said these hydration errors come from React rather than Next.js, so they converted the report to a discussion. One commenter shared a workaround that removes the attribute with a small script and a MutationObserver. Another suggested configuring ColorZilla to modify the page only when the user clicks the extension.
- **DevTools script in React:** React issue #25924 (opened in 2022, status unconfirmed) reports that a script the React DevTools extension injects after `<body>` triggers hydration warnings. The reporter asked whether `suppressHydrationWarning` should be applied to that injected script.
- **Recent React 19.2 report:** React issue #36169 is open and concerns `<script defer>` inside `<head>` causing hydration mismatches, even without extensions. It is listed as a React 19.2.4 bug.
- **Extension markup in dev overlays:** videospeed issue #1255 says a Video Speed Controller version adds a `class` to the `<html>` element and causes errors in the Next.js dev server. It quotes the React team's position that extensions should mostly avoid generating unexpected HTML. The exception is stray tags in `<head>` and `<body>`, which React 19 skips over.
- **Ignoring the error in Sentry:** Sentry issue #15886 reports that filtering the React 418 hydration error by message did not work in the Sentry Next.js SDK.
- **Recent app-level fixes:** Several pull requests from the past few weeks (suv27/Layer7-Siege #26, hiramustafabaig/GFX-T #11, connorpham/QC-Agent #7) suppress the warning on the root `<html>` or `<body>` element. They target extensions such as Grammarly, ColorZilla, and Material Design Lite. Each one is an application-level change, not an upstream fix.

content.text:
Yes. There are several threads, but I didn't find one canonical React issue that is resolved.

**Closest matches**
- [facebook/react #25924](https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/25924): "Scripts injected by browser extensions (e.g. React dev tools) may cause hydration errors." It was opened in 2022, so it isn't React 19-specific. It is the main upstream report on extension-injected markup.
- [vercel/next.js #72031](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/72031) and [discussion #72035](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/72035): the ColorZilla extension adds a `cz-shortcut-listen="true"` attribute to `<body>`, which triggers a hydration error in Next.js 15 with React 19. Next.js maintainers said the error comes from React and converted the issue to a discussion.
- [igrigorik/videospeed #1255](https://github.com/igrigorik/videospeed/issues/1255): the Video Speed Controller extension adds a `class` to `<html>`, which causes the error in the Next.js dev server.

**Related**
- [getsentry/sentry-javascript #15886](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry-javascript/issues/15886): filtering the React 19 hydration error out of Sentry.
- [facebook/react #36169](https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/36169): hydration mismatch on `<script defer>` in `<head>`. It doesn't involve extensions.

**Workarounds**
- Add `suppressHydrationWarning` to `<html>` or `<body>`.
- Disable the extension.
- Remove the injected attribute with a MutationObserver script, as one commenter on the ColorZilla thread suggested.

I only read the search result summaries, not the full threads, so I haven't checked the current status of each issue.
